annotations.description: DSV3 Analyst chose to take Beast Within with Thoughtseize from Qwen3L Dreamer's hand. While Beast Within is a versatile instant-speed removal spell that could threaten DSV3's permanents (including key enchantments like Pernicious Deed or Sylvan Library), Rishkar's Expertise is arguably the highest-impact card in the hand. Rishkar's Expertise can generate massive card advantage by drawing cards equal to greatest power AND casting a free spell with MV 5 or less. In a multiplayer game, denying that kind of card advantage engine is typically more impactful than removing a reactive removal spell. Rishkar, Peema Renegade is also notable as it enables mana ramp and enables Rishkar's Expertise to draw more cards. However, Beast Within is the card most likely to directly disrupt DSV3's game plan (destroying Pernicious Deed, Sylvan Library, or key lands), so there's a reasonable argument for taking it.

With Pernicious Deed in hand as a backup sweeper, removing the engine piece rather than the biggest body could be more impactful.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Whiptongue Hydra with Putrefy
annotations.betterLine: Target Kaima, the Fractured Calm with Putrefy to stop the snowballing +1/+1 counter engine, then use Pernicious Deed later if needed to clean up remaining threats

annotations.description: At 5 life, DSV3 Analyst tapped Cephalid Coliseum (which deals 1 damage to its controller) to pay the generic mana cost of Putrefy, unnecessarily losing 1 life to go to 4. They had multiple painless alternatives: Overgrown Tomb could produce {B}, Underground Sea could produce {B}, and Watery Grave could produce {B}, any combination of which could cover {1}{B}{G} without using Cephalid Coliseum.
annotations.actionTaken: Tapped Tropical Island for {G} and Cephalid Coliseum for generic mana ({U}), taking 1 damage at 5 life.
annotations.betterLine: Tap Tropical Island for {G}, Overgrown Tomb or Underground Sea for {B}, and any other untapped painless land for {1} generic, avoiding the 1 life loss from Cephalid Coliseum.

annotations.description: Sacrificed Rishkar, Peema Renegade to Sandfall Cell instead of a duplicate basic land. Rishkar provides mana acceleration (creatures with counters tap for G) and is a body, while sacrificing one of the duplicate Mountains or Forests would have minimal impact with 5 lands on board.
annotations.actionTaken: Sacrificed Rishkar, Peema Renegade (the player's reasoning was confused, thinking they were discarding from hand)
annotations.betterLine: Sacrifice a duplicate Mountain or Forest - losing 1 of 5 lands is far less impactful than losing a mana-producing creature that enables faster casting of Rishkar's Expertise and Collision of Realms

annotations.description: MiniMx Spike had to discard down to 7 cards at end of turn, suggesting they didn't use all their mana this turn. They could have added a storage counter to Saltcrusted Steppe during combat for free future value, since the mana ended up going unused.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Saltcrusted Steppe to add a storage counter.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Saltcrusted Steppe to add a storage counter ({1}, {T}), banking mana for future turns since the mana wasn't going to be spent anyway.

annotations.description: Sword of the Paruns is a slow equipment that requires significant additional mana investment (3 to equip, 3 to activate) and MiniMx Spike only has one creature (Hada Spy Patrol). Meanwhile, Acidic Slime is castable and would destroy Propaganda, which is actively taxing MiniMx Spike's attacks against Sonnet Story. Removing Propaganda while adding a 2/2 deathtouch body is far more impactful.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Sword of the Paruns (4 mana equipment with expensive activation costs)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Acidic Slime targeting Propaganda to remove the attack tax and add a relevant body to the board

annotations.description: Activating Sword of the Paruns to tap/untap the equipped creature during precombat main with no clear strategic purpose. With only Hada Spy Patrol on the battlefield and 8 lands available, this wastes 3 mana that could be used toward casting Darksteel Ingot (3 mana ramp/fixing) or Swiftfoot Boots (2 mana) to develop the board.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Sword of the Paruns' tap/untap ability for 3 mana with no apparent benefit.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Darksteel Ingot for mana ramp/fixing, or Swiftfoot Boots to prepare for future creature protection, or save the mana for other plays.

annotations.description: In a 1v1 against Sonnet Story with Propaganda up, MiniMx Spike spent mana leveling up Hada Spy Patrol (which already had hexproof from Swiftfoot Boots and was unblockable at level 1-2) instead of deploying Skyward Eye Prophets, a powerful card advantage engine that would help close out the game. The shroud from level 3 is largely redundant with hexproof from boots.
annotations.actionTaken: Leveled up Hada Spy Patrol to gain shroud (redundant with Swiftfoot Boots hexproof) instead of deploying a threat/engine.
annotations.betterLine: Play Island from hand, then cast Skyward Eye Prophets (3GWU) to establish a powerful card advantage engine for the 1v1 matchup against Sonnet Story.
